_comment: Source of truth for App Analytics campaign tokens for both Easy-Post apps.
Never type a token by hand: run `python packaging/campaign_links.py` and copy
'Site-EasyPost-Download' become two rows that will never be merged, and one
typo silently mints a third. That is the whole reason this file exists.
providerToken is shared across the ACCOUNT, not per app. Apple minted
129201947 on Wren's first campaign and returned the same value for both
Easy-Post apps afterwards, which is how we know. A new app therefore needs no
console step at all -- its links can be generated here directly.
One token per SURFACE, not per page and not per post. These are deliberately
coarse: a campaign shows no data at all until the app has been installed by
five individual Apple Accounts, so splitting finely now buys a screen of empty
rows. Split one when its volume justifies it, never before.
The easy-post site publishes into forty-odd language directories and every one
of them carries these App Store links. A token has to be applied across all of
them, not only the English page -- the same trap the favicon fell into.

campaigns.creative: Mac App Store button on the download page
campaigns.notes: Highest intent on the site. Created in the console first, so this is the link Apple itself returned.

campaigns.creative: Mac App Store button in the general site furniture
Mac App Store button on the three keyword landing pages
campaigns.notes: Kept together deliberately. These three are one acquisition channel and the question worth answering is whether search traffic converts at all, not which of the three does.

campaigns.creative: The bar above the header offering the Mac App Store
campaigns.notes: A different intent from the page buttons: it reaches somebody who came for something else and was offered the app.

campaigns.creative: App Store button on the companion's own page
campaigns.notes: Created in the console first, so this is the link Apple itself returned.

campaigns.surface: index.html, apps.html and the keyword landing pages
campaigns.creative: The "a companion iPhone app is also available" mentions inside desktop-facing pages
campaigns.notes: A different intent from mobile.html: these reach someone who came for the desktop app.

campaigns.creative: App Store button in the software site listing
campaigns.notes: The software site links the companion but NOT Easy-Post Desktop, so there is deliberately no matching desktop token.

campaigns.surface: site-wide app banner, iOS visitors not using Safari
campaigns.creative: The bar above the header offering the App Store
campaigns.notes: Same token as the macOS variant deliberately. It is one surface; Apple reports the two apps separately anyway.

campaigns.surface: Safari Smart App Banner, every page
campaigns.creative: Apple's own banner, drawn from the apple-itunes-app meta tag
campaigns.notes: Carried as affiliate-data on the meta tag, which is the documented form. UNVERIFIED against live data: campaigns report nothing until five Apple Accounts have installed, so this one has to be confirmed in App Analytics once volume exists.
